cards.name: hamming_weight_phasing_on_equal_angle_phase_gadgets
cards.identity: In a Hadamard-free segment of {cx, x, cz, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz}, every diagonal rotation acts as a phase gadget: up to global phase rz(a) on a wire carrying the GF(2) affine parity label p (a linear form over the segment's input Z-basis bits, tracked exactly as in pauli_frame_rotation_merge) contributes the phase e^{i a p}. Take any set of k >= 3 rotations inside one such segment whose angles are all equal to the SAME value a mod 2*pi (after normalizing a -> a mod 2*pi and folding a gadget with angle -a by replacing its parity label p with its complement p^1, which costs one x/global-phase bookkeeping, so +a and -a groups merge), with parity labels p_1..p_k (duplicates already merged by the existing rule, so the p_i are distinct). Their joint action is the phase e^{i a (p_1 + ... + p_k)} = e^{i a W}, W = integer Hamming weight of the bit string (p_1..p_k), 0 <= W <= k. Replace it by: (1) copy each p_i into a fresh clean ancilla a_i with CNOTs from the wires in the support of p_i (free, no T); (2) compute the binary representation W = sum_j 2^j w_j of the Hamming weight of a_1..a_k with a ripple network of (k - popcount(k)) full adders, each full adder being sum = a^b^c (3 CNOTs) and carry = MAJ(a,b,c) built from ONE Gidney AND gadget (4 T, |T> measured-uncompute form); (3) apply ceil(log2(k+1)) rotations rz(2^j * a) on the weight bits w_j; (4) uncompute the adder network by measured uncompute (0 T, Clifford + classically controlled CZ fix-ups) and uncopy the a_i with the same CNOTs, returning every ancilla to |0>. All k original rotations are deleted.
cards.correctness: Each gadget is diagonal in the computational basis of the segment's input, so all k commute and their product is a single diagonal operator |x> -> e^{i a sum_i p_i(x)}|x>; this is exactly the claimed phase on the integer W(x). The binary expansion W = sum_j 2^j w_j is exact over the integers, hence e^{i a W} = prod_j e^{i a 2^j w_j} = prod_j rz(2^j a) acting on the ancilla holding w_j, up to the fixed global phase bookkeeping of rz = diag(1, e^{i a}) vs diag(e^{-i a/2}, e^{i a/2}) (a global phase per rotation, unobservable). The parity labels p_i are computed into ancillas by CNOTs, which realize exactly the linear form over GF(2), and the full-adder network computes the Hamming weight exactly as a classical reversible circuit; Gidney's AND gadget computes a AND b into a clean |0> ancilla with 4 T and uncomputes it with an X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled CZ, exactly (not approximately). Signed folding is exact: rz(-a) on parity p = rz(a) on parity p^1 times a scalar e^{-i a}, because (-1)-weighting of a single bit equals weighting its complement up to a constant. So the whole replacement is unitary-equal to the original on the segment up to global phase, every ancilla starts and ends in |0>, and each measurement branch applies the same operator (the fix-ups are deterministic corrections), satisfying the relaxed contract's function + phase-consistency check exactly.
cards.trigger: Scan the op list into maximal Hadamard-free segments (split at every h and at any non-diagonal op touching a wire). Within a segment, propagate affine parity labels through cx/x (label of target ^= label of control; x flips the affine constant) and collect every t/tdg/rz with |angle mod 2*pi| not a multiple of pi/4 together with its parity label and position. Bucket these by normalized angle key: key = min(a mod 2*pi, 2*pi - (a mod 2*pi)) rounded to 1e-9, with the sign recorded so that a and -a land in the same bucket (the -a members get complemented labels). A match is a bucket with k >= 3 distinct parity labels whose rotations all lie in the same segment; emit buckets in decreasing k. On qae_13 the equal-angle buckets are the QAE/QPE controlled-phase cascade values pi/8, pi/16, pi/32, pi/64, pi/128, ... each appearing with multiplicity 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 as +a and the same multiplicities as -a (angles 12.173672 = -pi/8 mod 2*pi, 12.370021 = -pi/16, 12.468196 = -pi/32, ... in the histogram).
cards.expected_effect: The expensive objects are the 145 non-Clifford rotations, each synthesized by gridsynth at eps_rz = eps/N_Rz, i.e. roughly 3*log2(1/eps_rz) + c ~ 50 T each. Buckets of size k collapse to ceil(log2(k+1)) rotations at a T overhead of 4*(k - popcount(k)) for the AND gadgets. Taking the +/- folded buckets (sizes ~20, 18, 16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6 for pi/8 ... pi/1024, as many as survive the existing merge rule) the rotation count drops from ~90 surviving rotations to ~45-55, i.e. ~35-45 rotations removed at ~50 T each (~1800-2200 T) minus ~150-200 T of AND-gadget overhead; additionally N_Rz falling from ~90 to ~50 raises eps_rz from 6.9e-6 to ~1.2e-5, shaving ~2-3 T off every remaining rotation (~150 T more). Cost in space: ~k+log2(k) clean ancillas reused across buckets (buckets are processed one at a time, so ~20-24 extra qubits at peak, 13 -> ~35 qubits), and CNOT count rises by a few hundred. Net T on qae_13: 4527 -> ~3100-3300.
cards.source: Hamming weight phasing: Kivlichan, Gidney, Berry, Wiebe, McClean, Sun, Jiang, Rubin, Fowler, Aspuru-Guzik, Neven, Babbush, 'Improved Fault-Tolerant Quantum Simulation of Condensed-Phase Correlated Electrons via Trotterization', Quantum 4, 296 (2020), Sec. 'Hamming weight phasing'; the 4-T measured-uncompute AND gadget from C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018); phase-gadget/parity-label formalism from Kissinger & van de Wetering, 'Reducing the number of non-Clifford gates with spider nest identities / phase gadget synthesis' (2019).

cards.name: second_order_small_angle_rotation_commutation_merge
cards.identity: Normalize every rotation angle into (-pi, pi] modulo 2*pi first (the histogram contains 6.283952 = 2*pi + pi/4096, 12.564837 = 4*pi - pi/2048 etc., so 'small angle' and 'multiple of pi/4' must be decided after reduction). Propagate the Clifford frame exactly as pauli_frame_rotation_merge does, so the op list becomes a sequence of Pauli rotations R_{P_k}(theta_k) = exp(-i theta_k P_k / 2) followed by a final Clifford. Take a pair i < j with P_j = s * P_i (s = +-1), i.e. the pair the exact merge rule would fuse into R_{P_i}(theta_i + s*theta_j), but which the exact rule REFUSES because the intervening list contains rotations R_{Q_b}(phi_b) with {P_i, Q_b} = 0 (b in B, the blocker set; all non-anticommuting intervening rotations and Cliffords are passed exactly as today). Pick the member of the pair with the smaller |sin(angle/2)| (say j) and commute it across the blockers ANYWAY, i.e. replace the exact op list by the one in which R_{P_j}(theta_j) sits next to R_{P_i}(theta_i) and the two angles are added: R_{P_i}(theta_i + s*theta_j). Nothing else changes; the blockers, the Cliffords and all other rotations keep their order, gates and angles. This is an APPROXIMATION whose charged operator distance is second order (a product of sines of the two angles), unlike plain rotation truncation whose cost is first order in the angle; that is the whole point of the rule. Applications are emitted in decreasing order of (T removed) / (estimated distance) and applied greedily while the cumulative distance measured by the judge stays inside the remaining approx budget (5e-4).
cards.correctness: Write A = R_P(theta) = cos(theta/2) I - i sin(theta/2) P and B = R_Q(phi) = cos(phi/2) I - i sin(phi/2) Q with P, Q Paulis. Then [A, B] = -sin(theta/2) sin(phi/2) [P, Q]; if P and Q commute the commutator vanishes (exact swap, already exploited by the book rule), and if they anticommute then [P,Q] = 2PQ with PQ unitary, so ||A B - B A|| = 2 |sin(theta/2) sin(phi/2)|. Moving R_{P_j}(theta_j) across the blocker list one blocker at a time and using unitary invariance plus the triangle inequality gives the exact bound ||U_original - U_rewritten|| <= 2 |sin(theta_j/2)| * sum_{b in B} |sin(phi_b/2)|, and after the move P_j = s P_i so the two rotations are about the same axis and compose exactly: R_{P_i}(theta_i) R_{sP_i}(theta_j) = R_{P_i}(theta_i + s theta_j), which is an exact identity (R_{-P}(x) = R_P(-x)). Hence the rewrite is unitary-equal to the original up to an error bounded by the above product of sines, with no ancilla, no measurement and no qubit-count change; global phase is irrelevant because every factor is an SU(2)-type rotation about a Pauli. The bound is only an upper bound used for ranking - the judge's own phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window is the quantity charged to the ledger, so acceptance never depends on the bound being tight. Second order smallness: for theta_j = pi/2048 and three blockers of angle pi/8 the bound is 2*(7.7e-4)*(3*0.098) = 4.5e-4, whereas simply DELETING that same rotation (AQFT-style truncation) costs 2|sin(theta_j/4)| = 7.7e-4 on its own and buys only one rotation, so the same budget buys strictly more here.
cards.trigger: Scan the op list over {h, s, sdg, x, z, t, tdg, cx, cz, rz}. (1) Normalize each t/tdg/rz angle to (-pi, pi] mod 2*pi; drop anything that is already a multiple of pi/4 from the candidate set (those are Clifford/T and cheap). (2) For each remaining rotation k, propagate its Z axis backwards through the Cliffords to a common reference point with v3.api.pauli.conjugate, obtaining a signed Pauli P_k (this is the existing frame machinery; multi-qubit Z-type and X-type Paulis both occur here because of the 74 h gates). (3) For every pair i < j with P_j = +-P_i, let B = { intervening rotations b : anticommutes(P_i, P_b) } (use v3.api.pauli.commutes_with_z / the generic Pauli commutation test). If B is empty the exact book rule already handles it - skip. Otherwise emit the match (i, j, s, B) with estimated distance d = 2 * min(|sin(theta_i/2)|, |sin(theta_j/2)|) * sum_{b in B} |sin(phi_b/2)|, and estimated T saving = 50 if (theta_i + s*theta_j) mod 2*pi is not a multiple of pi/4, else about 100 (the surviving rotation also becomes Clifford/T). Order matches by saving/d descending and require d <= remaining budget. On qae_13 the candidates are exactly the +-pi/2^k pairs visible in the angle histogram (10 x +pi/8 vs 10 x -pi/8, 9 x +pi/16 vs 9 x -pi/16, ... 2 x +pi/2048 vs 2 x -pi/2048, plus the singletons pi/4096, pi/2048, ... hiding as 6.283952, 6.284719, ...): a +theta/-theta pair about the same frame Pauli sums to 0 and both rotations disappear, and the cheapest such pairs are those with the smallest |theta| and the fewest anticommuting blockers in between.
cards.expected_effect: Each surviving non-Clifford rotation costs about 3*log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 50 T at eps_rz = 5e-4/N_Rz. The exact book merge already removed the unblocked duplicates (6725 -> 4527, leaving roughly 90 rotations); what is left are same-axis pairs separated by anticommuting (H-induced, X-type-axis) rotations, which no exact ancilla-free pass can fuse. This rule spends the otherwise entirely unused approx half of the ledger (5e-4) on the cheapest of those fusions. Budget arithmetic on this circuit: one inverse pair at |theta| = pi/4096 or pi/2048 with one to three blockers costs 1.5e-4 to 4.5e-4 and removes BOTH rotations (sum 0 mod 2*pi), i.e. about 100 T for a quarter to all of the budget; pairs at pi/1024 with a single blocker cost about 3e-4 and also remove two rotations. Realistically 2 to 4 rotations disappear (one or two cheap pairs), 4527 -> about 4330-4430, plus a few T from N_Rz dropping (eps_rz rises slightly for everything that remains). The gain is deliberately modest and bounded by the 5e-4 budget, not by the number of matches: with a first-order mechanism (plain small-angle truncation) the same budget buys exactly ONE rotation (only pi/4096, cost 3.8e-4), so the second-order mechanism is worth about 2-4x more for the same error. No qubits added, CNOT count unchanged.
cards.source: Commutator norm bound for Pauli rotations: Childs, Su, Tran, Wiebe, Zhu, 'Theory of Trotter error with commutator scaling', PRX 11, 011020 (2021) (the ||[A,B]|| = 2|sin sin| estimate is the one-term case). Rotation merging / phase-polynomial frame propagation that this extends: Nam, Ross, Su, Childs, Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj Quantum Information 4, 23 (2018). Small-angle truncation as the first-order baseline it beats: Coppersmith, 'An approximate Fourier transform useful in quantum factoring' (1994); Barenco, Ekert, Suominen, Torma, 'Approximate quantum Fourier transform and decoherence', PRA 54, 139 (1996). Rotation cost model: Ross & Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16 (2016).
